intended_object: The canonical bijection F(A ×_X B) ≅ F(A) ×_{F(X)} F(B) = {(a,b) | F(f)(a) = F(g)(b)}, for a fiber functor F on a pre-Galois category. It expresses that fiber functors preserve pullbacks (from the docstring and name).
explanation:
The definition composes two isomorphisms. The first is `PreservesPullback.iso (F ⋙ FintypeCat.incl) f g`, which identifies the image of the pullback with the pullback of the images in `Type`. The second is `Types.pullbackIsoPullback`, which identifies a pullback in `Type` with the subtype `{p : A × B // f p.1 = g p.2}`. Together they give exactly the canonical bijection the docstring describes.

The companion lemmas `fiberPullbackEquiv_symm_fst_apply` and `fiberPullbackEquiv_symm_snd_apply` show that the inverse map is compatible with the two projections. So this is the canonical map, not just some bijection.

The only properties of the fiber functor it uses are that pullbacks exist and are preserved. These come from the Galois-category axioms, which are the setting of this API. It is a small convenience wrapper that specializes general Mathlib machinery to fiber functors. It does not re-implement a general construction, so it is not too narrow.
